messages:
maria: heads up, saw a p99 token tail spike on prod long-context traffic starting ~09:12 UTC. graphs show evict_count jumping and reuse_hit_rate dropping at the same time. attaching quick repro and profiler snippets.

james: which fleet/hostgroup? can you repro in staging?

maria: prod-a primarily, but i can repro locally with the long-context load generator (seq_len~32k). staging shows a smaller bump. repro script: `./tools/kv_repro.sh --length 32000 --concurrency 24`

li: evicter-bot fired earlier?

evicter-bot: ALERT: kv-evict-rate exceeded threshold on cluster prod-a at 09:11:48 UTC. recent commits: 4f2b3a9 -> 4f2b3b1 (kv: reuse reinsertion behavior change).

maria: confirmed correlation with commit 4f2b3b1 — that change made reuse path call `touch_entry()` which moves entries to MRU. hypothesis: reuse reinsertion + heavy long-context paging causes aliasing where hot prefixes get evicted when reused, leading to cascade.

ana: can we get a quick profile (userspace) around the eviction path? i want to see lock contention and expensive memmove ops.

maria: attached perf script output (filtered):
```
Samples: 120000 of event 'cycles'
  27.3%  runtime:kv_pager  [.] kv::pager::evict_batch
  16.8%  runtime:kv_cache  [.] kv::entry::touch_entry
  12.5%  libc-2.31.so  [.] memcpy
   8.2%  runtime:kv_cache  [.] kv::page::reclaim
```

james: memcpy is suspicious — are we shifting slab arrays on eviction? we copy lists on FIFO->LRU transitions?

li: also seeing a big spike in `kv::entry::touch_entry` which lines up with the reinsertion bump. if reinsertion is O(n) on long lists, that explains the memmove.

maria: code snippet (simplified):
```
fn touch_entry(e) {
  remove_from_list(e); // linear scan to unlink
  push_front(e);        // makes it MRU
}
```

ana: so moving entries on every reuse is heavy under long-context when list sizes grow. FIFO kept churn cheap (append-only) but LRU reinserts are costly. commit changed reuse to LRU semantics.

james: can we try a cheap experiment: flip policy to FIFO on a small canary and run the same load?

maria: did that on prod-a: flipped policy flag `kv.policy=fifo-append` on 3/4 nodes, p99 dropped from 410ms -> 130ms for token tail. reuse_hit_rate stabilized. evict_count unchanged but memcpy time disappeared. :thumbsup:

li: interesting. that means correctness was OK (no correctness regressions observed) but performance regressed due to reinsertion cost. any safety implications of FIFO?

maria: for our workload FIFO increases eviction locality (older entries evicted earlier) but we didn't see correctness issues for pinned contexts. we should audit pinned entry semantics.

ana: immediate action: revert the reuse-to-LRU change in 4f2b3b1 and land a targeted optimization: make touch_entry O(1) by using intrusive doubly-linked lists (store prev/next indexes in entry) or avoid unlink on reuse (fast-path bump flag). add a microbench for long lists.

james: also add a perf test that runs with seq_len=32k in CI perf lane and asserts that memcpy cycles < 5% and p99 < 200ms. 

maria: opened PR #6874 to revert + instrument. putting a canary rollout plan in the PR description.

li: followups:
- add unit test for reuse semantics (ensure reuse doesn't change ordering unless configured)
- add a safety toggle: `reuse_moves=true|false`
- long-term: consider hybrid policy: FIFO for very large caches, LRU for small caches.

ana: one more note — batching heuristics can amplify this: when we batch many requests that touch overlapping long prefixes, we produce many reuse events in a short window, increasing contention. need to ensure batching doesn't produce pathological reuse bursts.

maria: good call. i'll add a small limiter in batching layer to coalesce repeated touches into a single touch per cache-entry per batch. proving it reduces touch churn locally.

james: perfect. can we ship the revert now and follow up with the O(1) touch change?

maria: yes — reverting now. will monitor dashboards (p99 tokens, memcpy cycles, evicter alerts).

li: thanks everyone. can we also get a short postmortem once telemetry settles? just root cause and the perf regression link.

maria: will do. saving traces and profiler outputs to the incident runbook.

ana: assign follow-ups to eng-runtime board and tag release: 4f2b3b1-regress-evict. :white_check_mark:
